note: Install prompts on https://yulab-smu.top/Rho/. {folder} is the projects folder the visitor chose (default ~/rho-projects). Every command here was run on npm 0.5.3 in a throwaway HOME before publication; keep it that way when editing.

claude.label: Claude Code
claude.text:
Install Rho for me. It is a local workspace where you and I work on the same R projects; its guide is https://yulab-smu.top/Rho/docs/start/.

1. Run `node -v`. Rho needs Node 22.22 or a later 22.x. If this machine has another version, tell me how to get Node 22 and stop here.
2. Run `npm install -g @rho-workspace/rho`. If it fails with EACCES, explain my options instead of using sudo yourself.
3. Create {folder} for my projects. Start Rho so it keeps running after this conversation, with its service state outside that folder. On macOS or Linux: `nohup rho --root {folder} --state-dir ~/.rho-service --open > ~/.rho-service.log 2>&1 &`. On Windows, run the same rho command with full paths in its own PowerShell window. The log starts with a JSON line; tell me the url in it.
4. The first start copies an example project, PA14 quorum sensing, into {folder}. Read its README.md and tell me in three sentences what it studies.
5. Connect yourself to that project: run `rho --grant ~/.rho-service/connection.json --project "PA14 quorum sensing"`, then run the `claude mcp add` command it prints from inside the project folder. Tell me to start a new Claude Code session there to use Rho's tools.
6. Finish by telling me to open the url, choose PA14 quorum sensing and ask in Rho's Agent panel, and suggest three questions I could ask about the example.

codex.label: Codex
codex.text:
Install Rho for me. It is a local workspace where you and I work on the same R projects; its guide is https://yulab-smu.top/Rho/docs/start/.

1. Run `node -v`. Rho needs Node 22.22 or a later 22.x. If this machine has another version, tell me how to get Node 22 and stop here.
2. Run `npm install -g @rho-workspace/rho`. If it fails with EACCES, explain my options instead of using sudo yourself.
3. Create {folder} for my projects. Start Rho so it keeps running after this conversation, with its service state outside that folder and Codex as the Agent in its panel. On macOS or Linux: `nohup rho --root {folder} --state-dir ~/.rho-service --agent-backend codex-acp --open > ~/.rho-service.log 2>&1 &`. On Windows, run the same rho command with full paths in its own PowerShell window. The log starts with a JSON line; tell me the url in it.
4. The first start copies an example project, PA14 quorum sensing, into {folder}. Read its README.md and tell me in three sentences what it studies.
5. Connect yourself to that project: run `rho --grant ~/.rho-service/connection.json --project "PA14 quorum sensing"`. Its JSON names an `mcp` entry; add it with `codex mcp add <name> -- <command> <args>`. Tell me to start a new Codex session to use Rho's tools.
6. Finish by telling me to open the url, choose PA14 quorum sensing and ask in Rho's Agent panel, and suggest three questions I could ask about the example.
